quarterly_data.quarter: Hirata Corporation annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 consolidated results: net sales JPY 94,906,641 thousand (+7.3%), operating profit JPY 8,315 million (+20.5%), ordinary profit JPY 8,375 million (+21.6%), net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 6,077 million (+27.2%). Management states sales rose on production equipment for electric vehicles (EV) and internal combustion engines and on semiconductor wafer transfer equipment; semiconductor-related profit fell on delayed price pass-through, while automotive-related profit rose on appropriate pricing and higher proficiency. Segments: automotive-related net sales JPY 43,478 million (+1.0%), operating profit JPY 5,142 million (+22.6%), on large orders for engine and in-vehicle electronic component assembly equipment and steady battery charge / discharge equipment sales; semiconductor-related net sales JPY 36,106 million (+19.6%), operating profit JPY 2,418 million (-15.4%); other automated labor-saving equipment net sales JPY 12,572 million (-4.0%), operating profit JPY 669 million (turned profitable from an operating loss on an improved FPD equipment cost ratio).
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 94,906,641 thousand (+7.3%); operating profit JPY 8,315 million (+20.5%); net income JPY 6,077 million (+27.2%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Hirata Corporation annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor-related segment, fiscal year ended March 31, 2026: production JPY 36,613,001 thousand (111.2% of the prior year); orders received JPY 34,762,395 thousand (116.9%); order backlog JPY 17,670,308 thousand (92.9%); net sales JPY 36,106,069 thousand (119.6%). Management states sales held firm, centred on wafer transfer equipment, as generative AI-related orders continued, but profit fell on delayed price pass-through of cost increases, mainly purchased parts, and higher warranty costs on some products. Company-wide orders received JPY 90,270,045 thousand (113.5%) and order backlog JPY 51,796,746 thousand (91.8%); automotive-related orders JPY 42,341,859 thousand (124.1%), backlog JPY 29,065,597 thousand (96.2%).
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor orders JPY 34,762,395 thousand (116.9% of prior year); semiconductor backlog JPY 17,670,308 thousand (92.9%); total backlog JPY 51,796,746 thousand

quarterly_data.quarter: Hirata Corporation annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor capacity: under the mid-term plan the company is pursuing an approximately 50% increase in semiconductor production capacity and two new overseas production sites; it states that expanded overseas production bases in China and Malaysia and additional clean rooms are steadily increasing production capacity for component products and EFEMs. The semiconductor segment's operating margin was 6.7% in the fiscal year ended March 2026; the company aims to improve margin and capital efficiency by reviewing production control, optimising inventory and achieving appropriate pricing.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor production capacity: approximately 50% increase being pursued; 2 new overseas production sites; segment operating margin 6.7%

quarterly_data.quarter: Hirata Corporation annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Mid-term plan (the company's fiscal 2025-2027, i.e. the years ending March 2026 to March 2028) targets: operating profit of JPY 10 billion or more and ROE of 9.3% or more for the year ending March 2028, and a net sales CAGR of 6-8% over the plan period; first-year (fiscal year ended March 2026) results: sales CAGR 7.3%, operating margin 8.8%, ROE 8.4%. Other plan goals: an automotive-related operating margin of 10% or more (11.8% achieved after shifting to prioritise profit over sales volume), a roughly 20% shorter cash conversion cycle, and new businesses of JPY 5 billion or more in sales in each field, with the battery, control panel and electrification parts businesses targeted to become divisions in the company's fiscal 2027 (the year ending March 2028).
quarterly_data.figure: Operating profit target JPY 10 billion or more (year ending March 2028); ROE 9.3% or more; sales CAGR 6-8%

quarterly_data.quarter: Hirata Corporation annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management states that in the semiconductor market, data-center investment demand driven by the rapid spread of generative AI is expected to keep the market expanding; in automotive, BEV investment has partly slowed since late 2023 while ICE and HEV capital investment remains firm, and in Japan powertrain capital investment including HV and PHV is expected to become active. It says energy prices, inflation and exchange rates driven by geopolitical risk are raising procurement and labour costs, and it is pursuing appropriate pricing.

quarterly_data.quarter: Hirata Corporation annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capital expenditure in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 totalled JPY 3,847 million, mainly construction of the Shichijo No. 2 Plant (JPY 2,005 million), a new plant at subsidiary Taihei Technos (JPY 428 million), a new core IT system (JPY 210 million) and paving at the Kanto Plant (JPY 50 million). R&D expenses totalled JPY 1,561 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 3,847 million; R&D JPY 1,561 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Hirata Corporation annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New facility plans: the Shichijo No. 2 Plant (Kikuchi, Kumamoto; production plant serving the automotive, semiconductor and other segments), planned investment JPY 2,450,000 thousand, of which JPY 1,850,000 thousand paid, started May 2025, completion scheduled June 2026; Taihei Technos production plant (Kita-ku, Kumamoto), planned investment JPY 790,000 thousand, of which JPY 472,464 thousand paid, started February 2024, completion scheduled June 2026. The company acquired the Shichijo No. 2 Plant in the fiscal year ended March 2026 for the expansion of its mass-production business and began partial operation in May 2026; it plans to consolidate its production bases in Kumamoto Prefecture to raise production efficiency.
quarterly_data.figure: Shichijo No. 2 Plant JPY 2,450,000 thousand (completion June 2026); Taihei Technos plant JPY 790,000 thousand (completion June 2026)

quarterly_data.quarter: Hirata Corporation annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D: in semiconductors, the company says demand for semiconductor products is rising with active investment in generative AI and automotive applications, and it is developing high-value-added load ports, atmospheric and vacuum wafer transfer robots, EFEMs integrating them and PLP-related equipment to customer-specific needs and SEMI standards. In industrial robots, with the share of robots for semiconductor manufacturing equipment rising, it is taking on customer-specific development projects. In medical equipment it has developed a system in which a physician operates a robot carrying a focused-ultrasound device to ablate cancer and is now developing the mass-production model and building a production system.
